text:
CORRECTION AND EXTENSION of my earlier reference on this bead. My first pass tested the NULL only, and concluded "no detectable leakage at any shrinkage level". That conclusion was incomplete. Under SIGNAL the two policies differ materially.

Full criterion-3 quantities, paired across policies on identical noise draws. reps=400, shrinkage=0.05, n=48, p=12, R=4 runs, base R, no package code.

NULL (population target 0.000000)
  train-only  mean +0.000278  bias_vs_pop +0.000278  bias_vs_cond +0.000000  var 1.222e-04  RMSE 0.011042  MCse 0.000553
  all-runs    mean +0.000278  bias_vs_pop +0.000278  bias_vs_cond +0.000000  var 9.859e-05  RMSE 0.009921  MCse 0.000496
  paired diff mean -0.000000  MCse 0.000141  z -0.00   90% CI [-0.000232, +0.000231]

SIGNAL (population target 0.033992)
  train-only  mean +0.035107  bias_vs_pop +0.001115  bias_vs_cond +0.002993  var 3.979e-04  RMSE 0.019953  MCse 0.000997
  all-runs    mean +0.033078  bias_vs_pop -0.000914  bias_vs_cond +0.000965  var 3.331e-04  RMSE 0.018252  MCse 0.000913
  paired diff mean -0.002028  MCse 0.000207  z -9.81  90% CI [-0.002369, -0.001688]

So: under the null the policies are equivalent to within +/-0.00023 at 90% confidence. Under signal they differ at z = -9.81, and in opposite directions relative to the population target - train-only biased +0.0011 high, all-runs -0.0009 low. all-runs also has lower variance (3.33e-4 vs 3.98e-4) and lower RMSE (0.0183 vs 0.0200).

THE MECHANISM IS LEARNER QUALITY, NOT LEAKAGE - which is exactly the distinction acceptance criterion 5 asks for.

With R=4 runs, excluding both evaluated runs leaves the training-only policy TWO runs of residuals; the all-runs policy uses FOUR. So the two policies do not differ only in provenance, they differ in how much data estimates Sigma_hat. A noisier Sigma_hat inverts to a systematically larger K, which inflates the estimate - hence train-only sitting high. Under the null this cannot show, because delta_a and delta_b are independent of Sigma_hat and the expectation is zero however noisy the metric is. The bias_vs_cond column, measured against the TRUE metric, confirms it: train-only overshoots by 0.0030, all-runs by 0.0010, roughly a 3x ratio.

CONSEQUENCES FOR THIS EPIC

- The honest conclusion is not "the policies are equivalent". It is: equivalent under the null, materially different under signal, with the difference attributable to Sigma_hat precision rather than evaluation-data contamination.
- That triggers your last acceptance criterion - a material policy difference must become a durable evidence report and a follow-up research issue, not a hidden default.
- The confound is fixable and worth separating: to isolate provenance from data volume, compare all-runs against a training-only policy matched on the NUMBER of training runs (for example R=6 with 4 training runs in both arms). Whatever difference survives that is provenance; what disappears is learner quality.
- My equivalence-margin advice still applies, but only to the null arm. The signal arm needs a difference report, not an equivalence claim.
